en: It's great to be here.

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, Jensen.

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, for the students who only know NVIDIA as a company at the center of AI, what part of the early NVIDIA story do they most need to understand?
zh: 那么，对于那些只把 NVIDIA 视为一家处于 AI 中心的公司的人来说，他们最需要了解 NVIDIA 早期故事的哪个部分？

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that most people don't believe is that the choice of our technology that we started the company with was absolutely wrong.
zh: 大多数人不相信的是，我们创办公司时选择的技术绝对是错误的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had started with the idea that we would reinvent 3D graphics.
zh: 我们最初的想法是，我们要重新发明 3D 图形。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the company's philosophy and perspective was that the general purpose computers, the CPUs, were really useful, but if we could augment it with accelerators, we could solve problems that otherwise too hard to solve.
zh: 公司的哲学和观点是，通用计算机、CPU 非常有用，但如果我们能用加速器增强它，我们就能解决原本太难解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the first problems we chose was 3D graphics.
zh: 我们选择的第一个问题之一就是 3D 图形。

speaker: Unknown
en: And during that time, 1993, the PC was just rumored to be coming.
zh: 在那个时代，1993 年，PC 还只是传闻即将到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our big idea was that we would turn every single personal computer into a game console, because we grew up in the era of game consoles.
zh: 我们的想法是，我们将把每一台个人电脑变成游戏机，因为我们在游戏机时代长大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we thought, you know, what if we could design a system that would fit into the personal computer and it would turn it into a game console.
zh: 所以我们认为，如果我们能设计一个适合放入个人电脑的系统，并将它变成游戏机会怎么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we thought we would reinvent the algorithm that would require these large supercomputers and we would fit it into the PC.
zh: 我们认为我们将重新发明需要这些大型超级计算机的算法，并将其放入 PC 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we came up with some new algorithms.
zh: 我们想出了一些新算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: The more we were excited about it, we believed in it.
zh: 我们越兴奋，就越相信它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We reasoned about it in a thoughtful way.
zh: 我们以深思熟虑的方式对其进行了推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we went to start the company to go build it.
zh: 我们去创办公司来构建它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it turns out the algorithm was exactly wrong.
zh: 结果证明该算法是完全错误的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the technology that founded the company turns out to be exactly wrong.
zh: 公司所基于的技术结果证明是完全错误的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in 1995, we realized that, and it was almost too late, because by then, there were some 35, 40 other companies that were building 3D graphics for PCs.
zh: 所以在 1995 年，我们意识到了这一点，当时几乎太晚了，因为那时已经有大约 35、40 家其他公司在为 PC 构建 3D 图形。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we realized that it didn't work, and I went back to the company, and we were at the company, and I said, what are we going to do?
zh: 所以我们意识到它行不通，我回到公司，我们在公司里，我说，我们要怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't work, and we were all talking about it.
zh: 它行不通，我们都在讨论这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, look, we...
zh: 我说，听着，我们……

speaker: Unknown
en: we won't have a company if we don't confront the fact that this doesn't work and start working towards the right algorithm.
zh: 如果我们不面对它行不通这一事实并开始朝着正确的算法努力，我们就不会有公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then somebody told me, it turns out none of us knew how to do it the right way.
zh: 然后有人告诉我，结果我们中没有人知道如何以正确的方式做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not only did we choose the wrong technology, we didn't know how to do it the right way.
zh: 我们不仅选择了错误的技术，而且我们不知道如何以正确的方式做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was a big day for me.
zh: 所以对我来说，那是重要的一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had a couple of $60, a couple of $100 in my pocket.
zh: 我口袋里有几张 60 美元，几张 100 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I went down to Fry's and I bought three textbooks.
zh: 所以我去了 Fry's 并买了三本教科书。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the textbooks was about OpenGL and how to design OpenGL pipelines.
zh: 教科书是关于 OpenGL 以及如何设计 OpenGL 流水线的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I brought it back to the company and gave it to the engineers.
zh: 我把它带回公司并交给了工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here we are.
zh: 我们走到了今天。

speaker: Unknown
en: We reinvented computer graphics.
zh: 我们重新发明了计算机图形学。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're the world leader in modern computer graphics.
zh: 我们是现代计算机图形学的世界领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We invented most of the major breakthroughs in the last 25 years.
zh: 我们发明了过去 25 年中的大部分重大突破。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody would have thought that NVIDIA started out as world leaders in 3D graphics.
zh: 每个人都会认为 NVIDIA 最初就是 3D 图形的世界领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we learned it from a textbook.
zh: 我们是从教科书中学到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we actually started the company, raised money, and bought textbooks when you think about it.
zh: 所以我们实际上创办了公司，筹集了资金，并买了教科书，当你仔细想的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the big lesson is that, for me, is technology is changing all the time.
zh: 所以对我而言，重要的教训是，技术一直在变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so long as you're able to confront the reality, so long as you are able to learn, the technology itself actually doesn't matter.
zh: 只要你能够面对现实，只要你能够学习，技术本身其实并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so since then, NVIDIA has been inventing all kinds of technology since, all kinds of technology we've never really done before.
zh: 所以从那时起，NVIDIA 发明了各种各样的技术，发明了我们以前从未真正做过的各种技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we approach everything with the same attitude.
zh: 我们用同样的态度处理一切事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's important to do, we're going to go learn it, and how hard can it be?
zh: 如果这件事很重要，我们就去学习它，能有多难呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it always turns out to be much, much harder than...
zh: 结果总是比……

speaker: Unknown
en: than we expect, but you go into it with the attitude, how hard can it be?
zh: 比我们预期的要难得多，但你带着一种态度进入它，能有多难呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, backstage we were talking about how, I mean, we were talking with some of the top YC companies and you were saying that each one
zh: 我的意思是，在后台我们在谈论如何，我的意思是，我们在与一些顶级的 YC 公司交谈，你在说每一个

speaker: Unknown
en: has expertise in a domain that you and NVIDIA have an expertise in.
zh: 都拥有你和 NVIDIA 擅长的领域的专业知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're all just, I forget what you said, it was like an algorithmic domain of a sort.
zh: 它们都只是，我忘了你说什么了，就像某种算法领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it sounds like 3D graphics was merely the first of an algorithmic domain.
zh: 所以听起来 3D 图形学似乎只是一个算法领域的开端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it came from a textbook, but then anyone could have read that textbook.
zh: 它来自一本教科书，但任何人都可能读过那本教科书。

speaker: Unknown
en: You created- Particle physics, fluid dynamics, yeah.
zh: 你创造了——粒子物理、流体动力学，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: that you created the thing that people want, like the end product that people want to pay a lot of money for.
zh: 你创造了人们想要的东西，就像人们愿意花很多钱购买的最终产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: The big idea of the company that was spot on is that it is possible to augment the CPU to solve problems that otherwise are too difficult to solve.
zh: 公司的那个完全正确的大理念是，可以通过增强 CPU 来解决否则太难解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And molecular dynamics is one of them.
zh: 分子动力学就是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Image processing is one of them.
zh: 图像处理就是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Inverse physics is another one.
zh: 逆向物理是另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so all kinds of different algorithms, of course, deep learning is one of the major ones.
zh: 所以各种不同的算法，当然，深度学习是主要算法之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order to create the company that we have today, we realized early on that it's not about building a great chip, it's about accelerating an algorithm domain.
zh: 为了打造我们今天的公司，我们很早就意识到，这不仅仅是为了制造一块很棒的芯片，而是为了加速一个算法领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the things that I've always believed in is what makes great companies is a unique perspective about the world that you deeply believe in.
zh: 所以我一直相信的一点是，成就伟大的公司是对世界的一种独特的视角，并且你深信不疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not so much the technology, it's not so much the market even.
zh: 这不完全是技术，甚至也不完全是市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those things all matter.
zh: 这些事情都很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you have the right technology for the right market at the right time, your life is going to be a lot easier.
zh: 如果你在正确的时间为正确的市场拥有正确的技术，你的生活将会容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: A high-level vision about the future of some important thing, a perspective about it that's somehow unique.
zh: 对某个重要事情的未来有一个高层次的愿景，有一个关于它的某种独特的视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: that you deeply believe in.
zh: 并且你深信不疑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ideally, pursuing that vision is hard to do.
zh: 理想情况下，追求这个愿景是难以做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are kind of good combinations.
zh: 这些都是很好的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our case, we realized that accelerated computing was gonna be important.
zh: 就我们的情况而言，我们意识到加速计算将会很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And accelerated computing turns out to be very important.
zh: 而加速计算结果确实非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our realization is everything to do with algorithm, not the chip, turns out to be exactly right.
zh: 我们的感悟是，一切都与算法有关，而不是芯片，结果证明是完全正确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've said a lot about, I guess, the hardships of a founder.
zh: 所以你说了很多关于，我想，创始人的艰辛。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there a few stories that really jump out at you?
zh: 有没有什么故事真正让你印象深刻？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the people in this room would love to start a company, but are they really prepared for eating glass and possibly having to shut down the company, like things going wrong?
zh: 我的意思是，这个房间里的人都想创办一家公司，但他们真的准备好吃玻璃和可能不得不关闭公司了吗，就像事情出了错一样？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the pivotal moments that really jump out at you?
zh: 有哪些关键时刻真正让你印象深刻？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you were just in Japan, right?
zh: 我想你刚才去了日本，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you were sort of honoring Sega, was it?
zh: 你在致敬世嘉，是吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I feel like that was a really powerful story.
zh: 所以我觉得那是一个非常有力的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The project that led us to realize the algorithm we chose was wrong was a partnership with Sega.
zh: 导致我们意识到我们选择的算法是错误的项目是与世嘉的合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sega had contracted us to build the game console after Saturn that turned out to have been Dreamcast.
zh: 世嘉已经签约委托我们在土星之后构建游戏机，结果是 Dreamcast。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does anybody know what Dreamcast is?
zh: 有人知道 Dreamcast 是什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we did not build Dreamcast.
zh: 所以我们没有构建 Dreamcast。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were originally supposed to build Dreamcast.
zh: 我们最初应该构建 Dreamcast。

speaker: Unknown
en: But because our algorithm and our technology was fundamentally flawed, I went to Japan and I told Irimanji-san, the CEO at the time, that the contract that they gave us was like $12 million contract.
zh: 但是因为我们的算法和我们的技术从根本上是有缺陷的，我去了日本并告诉当时的 CEO Irimanji 先生，他们给我们的合同大约是一份 1200 万美元的合同。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will not be able to fulfill because the technology doesn't work.
zh: 我们将无法履行，因为技术不起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I told him the reasons why.
zh: 我告诉了他原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I advised that they choose somebody else to do it.
zh: 然后我建议他们选择别人来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then I asked him, I told him that I unfortunately still need the money.
zh: 但后来我问他，我告诉他不幸的是我仍然需要这笔钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he asked me, you know, the conference, you could just imagine the conversation.
zh: 他问我，你知道的，会议，你可以想象那次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what you're telling me is what I contract you to do, you can't do, but you would like all the money on the contract.
zh: 所以你告诉我的是，我签约让你做这件事，你做不到，但你想要合同上的所有钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I said, you got it.
zh: 我说，你说对了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's exactly right.
zh: 那完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: But obviously I was polite.
zh: 但显然我当时很礼貌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was, I was humble.
zh: 我很谦逊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he realized that, that I was honest and, and, and,
zh: 他意识到了，我是诚实的，并且，并且，并且，

speaker: Unknown
en: And everything made sense.
zh: 一切都说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if he didn't give us the money, we'd be out of business.
zh: 如果他不给我们这笔钱，我们就会倒闭。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that this happens in this room.
zh: 我认为这在这个房间里也会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't invest in companies, you invest in people.
zh: 你不投资公司，你投资的是人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what Irmajuri recognized was here's somebody and a company that he trusted in the first place, the contract, and that he believed in.
zh: Irmajuri 认识到的是，这里有一个人和一个公司，是他首先信任的，那份合同，并且他相信的。

speaker: Unknown
en: and that he would love to see make it to the next day.
zh: 并且他很高兴看到它能撑到第二天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that $5 million kept us alive and gave me enough time to discover what to do.
zh: 所以那 500 万美元让我们活了下来，并给了我足够的时间去发现该做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I guess they sold it for $15 million, I heard.
zh: 然后我猜他们把它卖了 1500 万美元，我听说的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, they sold it the moment we went public.
zh: 是的，我们一上市他们就把它卖了。

speaker: Unknown
en: When NVIDIA went public, our valuation was $300 million.
zh: 当 NVIDIA 上市时，我们的估值是 3 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: $300 million in 1999.
zh: 1999 年的 3 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was real money.
zh: 那可是真金白银。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's north of a trillion dollars now or so.
zh: 我想现在超过一万亿美元左右了吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more than true, yeah.
zh: 不仅如此，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, that's wild.
zh: 是的，太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're sort of the core, you know, we like to say that you're the man who controls the spice.
zh: 所以你是核心，你知道，我们喜欢说你是一个控制香料的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, before that, I don't think anyone could have really predicted per se how important...
zh: 在那之前，我认为没有人能够真正预测你所构建的技术……

speaker: Unknown
en: and the technology you built would be for this AI revolution.
zh: 对这场 AI 革命会有多么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you see?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, was it the accelerator and being in the right place at the right time?
zh: 我的意思是，是那个加速器并在正确的时间出现在正确的地点吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or surely there were a lot of things that led up to that that allowed you to sort of capture this position.
zh: 还是肯定有很多事情促成了这一点，让你能够占据这个位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw AlexNet just like everybody else saw AlexNet.
zh: 我像其他人看到 AlexNet 一样看到了 AlexNet。

speaker: Unknown
en: And...
zh: 而且……

speaker: Unknown
en: But remember, our lens of the world, my view of the world, was always looking for algorithms.
zh: 但请记住，我们看世界的透镜，我看世界的方式，总是在寻找算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the algorithm could be NAMD, the algorithm could be VASP, the algorithm could be OpenGL.
zh: 算法可能是 NAMD，算法可能是 VASP，算法可能是 OpenGL。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be SQL, some domain-specific language, some algorithm.
zh: 它可能是 SQL，某种领域特定语言，某种算法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my lens of the world was always looking for some problem that we might be able to help solve.
zh: 所以我看世界的透镜总是在寻找我们可能帮助解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: When AlexNet came along, the algorithm was deep learning.
zh: 当 AlexNet 出现时，算法就是深度学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question is, what is this algorithm?
zh: 所以问题是，这个算法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And why does it matter?
zh: 为什么它很重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why was it so effective?
zh: 为什么它如此有效？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what else can it do?
zh: 它还能做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you were to scale algorithms and scale it beyond that, what could it solve that otherwise you can't solve today?
zh: 如果你扩展算法并超越那个规模，它能解决哪些今天 otherwise 你无法解决的问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the breakthrough for us was realizing that AlexNet was not AlexNet, that AlexNet was an approach with deep learning that allows you to learn any function.
zh: 对我们的突破是意识到 AlexNet 不是 AlexNet，AlexNet 是一种深度学习的方法，允许你学习任何函数。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so 15 years ago, I was telling everybody that, hey, guess what?
zh: 所以 15 年前，我告诉大家，嘿，你猜怎么着？

speaker: Unknown
en: We just learned the universal function approximator.
zh: 我们刚刚学习了通用函数近似器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just discovered the universal function approximator.
zh: 我们刚刚发现了通用函数近似器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We could give it the answer for almost any function, and it could learn what the function is.
zh: 我们可以给它几乎任何函数的答案，它可以学习该函数是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for a lot of functions, you don't have to be precise.
zh: 对于许多函数，你不必很精确。

en: And in fact, it's impossible to be precise.
zh: 事实上，不可能很精确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so most of the interesting problems are imprecise in this way.
zh: 所以大多数有趣的问题都是这样不精确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so,
zh: 所以，

speaker: Unknown
en: The day that we realized we have a universal function approximator, the question then is, what does that do to the computing stack?
zh: 我们意识到拥有通用函数近似器的那一天，问题就变成了，这对计算堆栈有什么作用？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that happen to software?
zh: 对软件会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the industries that this could impact?
zh: 这可能影响哪些行业？

speaker: Unknown
en: So on and so forth.
zh: 等等。
